transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-11 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sasha Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO, Finovate), Priya Rao (Head of ML), Ethan Brooks (SRE), Nora Kim (Product)

[00:00] Sasha: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Sasha from Redwood, and Maya's here from the engineering team. Quick check - did we want to run through the canary plan then the runbook items?
[00:22] Liam: Yeah that sounds good, been looking forward to nailing down the cutover. We've got staging traffic routed this morning, so we can be pretty pragmatic.
[00:35] Maya: Great. Quick note, our proposed canary is 5% traffic for two weeks with automated rollback if P95 latency increases by >25% or error rate crosses 0.5% for five minutes. That's the starting point.
[00:50] Priya: 5% seems reasonable, but can we do a stepped ramp, like 1% for 24 hours, then 5% steady? Also for the latency metric, our baseline P95 is around 220ms, so a 25% hit is quite big for us.
[01:08] Sasha: Yeah totally, we can do step ramping. The thresholds are configurable — Maya, maybe note that down as a recommendation: 1% -> 5% -> 10% after two days, only if SLOs hold.
[01:24] Maya: noted. Also, we want to call out cost impact if you choose Dedicated GPUs for the canary vs Hosted. Dedicated gives more predictable latency but of course there's reserved cost. We can compute incremental cost for the canary window.
[01:40] Ethan: On the SRE side, main ask is clear rollback criteria and the runbook steps. We need to know what logs look like, where to find the KV cache hit metrics — sorry K V cash, the transcript tool sometimes writes it funny — and how to trigger a manual failover to the previous model.
[02:02] [laughter] Maya: yeah the transcript gods... For KV cache, we'll include the metric names and dashboard links in the runbook. Manual failover is an API call in the control plane, we'll document it.
[02:18] Nora: also curious about data residency — during canary will any tokens or user data be persisted outside our VPC? We need that answered before go-live.
[02:30] Sasha: Good point. For Dedicated it's all in your VPC, no external persistence. For Hosted, we can enable customer data isolation features and limited retention — but we'll send the precise data flow diagram.
[02:46] Liam: I want to make sure SOC2 and KMS integration checks are in the checklist. We have an internal audit week of 2026-11-30 so ideally we have the compliance artifacts by then.
[02:58] Sasha: We'll share the SOC2 summary and KMS integration notes. Maya, add that as an action to share docs.
[03:10] Maya: Added. On monitoring, we recommend these: P95 latency, P50 latency, token throughput, request error rate, model confidence degradation (if you have a scoring), and typical keys: kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size_avg. We'll provide a Grafana dashboard and alerts tuned to those thresholds.
[03:30] Priya: For model quality, can we run automatic A/B comparisons on outputs for a random 0.5% of traffic and send diffs to our eval pipeline? We want to catch semantic regressions not just latency.
[03:44] Maya: Yes, Redwood's routing supports shadowing 0.5% of traffic for A/B evaluation; we can set up a side-by-side compare and send diffs to your eval webhook. That will not affect latency.
[03:56] Liam: Ok so to summarize the canary flow: step ramp 1% -> 5% -> 10% if metrics hold, 2 week window with automated rollback triggers on latency and errors, shadowing 0.5% for A/B quality checks, manual failover API for SREs, and dedicated monitoring dashboards. Anything missing?
[04:18] Sasha: We should also call out runbook roles — who acknowledges alerts, who executes rollback, escalation path to Redwood. Maybe we map that in a small table in the runbook.
[04:30] Ethan: For SREs, our oncall will acknowledge and if it's a false positive they can silence alerts; rollback requires approval from our oncall lead plus a Redwood engineer. We want the steps short so they can do it in <10 minutes.
[04:46] Maya: We'll draft a one-page runbook with tl;dr and step-by-step commands: check dashboard, check KV cache hit, check request trace, call failover API, notify stakeholders.
[04:58] Priya: And include quality gate checks too — if A/B diff score crosses threshold, that's a soft stop and we escalate to manual review.
[05:08] Sasha: Good. On the Dedicated vs Hosted cost question — for the canary window, Dedicated reserved capacity for a short time can be expensive. We can also reserve a small Dedicated pool or run on Hosted but pin to a high-priority lane; Maya, can you put some numbers?
[05:25] Maya: I will. I'll run three scenarios: Hosted with premium priority, Dedicated small pool for canary, and hybrid where we route only critical traffic to Dedicated. I'll include estimated token cost and hourly reserved cost.
[05:38] Liam: Another item — traceability and audit logs. We need request-level logs with redaction to match our compliance policy. Does Redwood keep audit logs for control-plane actions?
[05:50] Sasha: Yes, we provide audit logs for control-plane events and request-level metadata can be exported to your logging bucket with PII redaction options. We'll send the configuration guide.
[06:04] Nora: In terms of timeline, we want a canary kickoff by the week of Nov 23. That gives time for the audit week and runbook review.
[06:16] Sasha: Sounds feasible. Action items recap at the end. Before we wrap, any blocking concerns?
[06:25] Priya: Only that we need the A/B evaluation webhook enabled and the diff scoring thresholds defined. I'll share our scoring rubric in a follow-up.
[06:36] Ethan: On the networking side, we need a test VPC peering and sample logs to validate the runbook steps. We'll do that by Nov 20.
[06:45] Maya: perfect. We'll also include a cutover checklist: pre-cutover smoke tests (5 minute low-latency checks), canary health checks, and final cutover plan for moving to 100% which will be manual with a 1-hour observation window.
[07:03] Liam: For the final cutover, if all canary metrics are green for 72 hours at 10% we can approve a staged ramp to 100% with a 1-hour hold at 50%. Make that explicit.
[07:16] Sasha: we'll add that. Any competitor concerns? Liam: we evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI for latency but Redwood's routing and caching is attractive. We still need to see hard numbers.
[07:30] Sasha: We'll include benchmark numbers and our sample perf spreadsheet.
[07:36] [crosstalk]
[07:40] Maya: Ok last admin, I'll send the runbook draft and Grafana links by Nov 18. Sasha will send cost scenarios and canary doc by Nov 13.
[07:52] Sasha: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the canary kickoff and attach all artifacts.
[08:00] Liam: thanks all, good session.

Meeting end.
